claims.text: Superconducting behavior in conventional high-entropy alloys is primarily governed by electron–phonon coupling strength.
Atomic size mismatch induces local lattice distortions in high-entropy alloys.
Local lattice distortions modulate electron–phonon coupling strength.
Using constituent elements with more similar atomic radii will reduce local lattice distortions.
Reducing local lattice distortions will strengthen effective electron–phonon coupling and raise Tc.
Homogeneous, equiatomic or near-equiatomic ReCrFeCoNi-based solid solutions can exhibit conventional superconductivity.
Element substitution can systematically reduce atomic size mismatch while overall valence electron count and phase stability are held constant.
Resistivity, magnetic susceptibility, and specific-heat measurements can determine the superconducting transition temperature.
Atomic-size-induced lattice distortions affect the phonon spectrum.
Atomic-size-induced lattice distortions affect the density of states at the Fermi level.
Changes in phonon modes caused by local distortion alter electron–phonon coupling.
Electron–phonon coupling is a critical factor in conventional superconductivity.
Greater disorder can increase electron scattering and weaken electron–phonon coupling.
Samples with less lattice distortion will have a measurably higher Tc than baseline alloys with greater atomic size mismatch.
The reduction in measured lattice distortion will correlate positively with the increase in Tc.
The proposed relationship is limited to single-phase solid-solution HEAs dominated by conventional electron–phonon pairing.
The proposed relationship may fail in phase-segregated systems or systems dominated by unconventional pairing.
Residual disorder, density-of-states changes, and phonon-spectrum changes may counteract or complicate the predicted Tc enhancement.
High-resolution XRD peak broadening and TEM analysis can provide quantitative metrics of local lattice distortion.
Failure of reduced distortion to increase Tc, or absence of a significant distortion–Tc correlation, would falsify the hypothesis.
